## Hierarchical VPS runtime configuration

- Config → Per-VPS is now a server-owned hierarchy instead of a blank
  incremental TOML textarea. It presents inherited values, explicit VPS
  overrides, ownership, locks, and final desired values in one searchable tree.
- Operators can add, edit, remove, inherit, reorder, or explicitly empty the
  supported value at its actual path. Changes remain staged until server
  preview, privilege confirmation, and one compare-and-set apply.
- Advanced mode edits the same complete sparse per-VPS override as TOML. Bulk
  VPS override patch remains a separate incremental language with explicit
  field/table deletion, frozen reviewed targets, and one atomic override write.
- Invalid Advanced text remains intact locally for repair; a valid reviewed
  replacement is stored as canonical TOML, so comments and source formatting
  are not persistence semantics.
- Optional ConfigRead evidence compares the running agent with the last saved
  desired configuration. Unsaved draft changes remain visually separate from
  operational drift.

## Runtime identity boundary

- VPS display names and tags are now exclusively server inventory. They are no
  longer copied into agent runtime configuration, runtime hashes, ConfigRead
  output, apply-state JSON, or command argument expansion.
- ConfigRead returns a structured, runtime-only, credential-redacted document.
  RuntimeConfigSync and ConfigRead now require configuration command protocol
  v3; the agent update command remains available across the cutover.
- A verified legacy agent cache is decoded without losing valid tunnel and
  runtime state, marked for authoritative synchronization, and rewritten in the
  clean format only after a successful v3 acknowledgement.

## Review and mutation integrity

- Single-VPS replacement and Bulk incremental mutation now have explicit
  preview/apply APIs. Preview hashes bind the exact candidate, desired-state
  basis, and target IDs; apply verifies operator privilege and rechecks the
  reviewed state under repository locks before any override is committed.
- Malformed historical overrides remain visible and can be repaired by an
  explicit single-VPS replacement or reset. Bulk refuses to mutate a malformed
  target because it cannot safely preserve omitted fields.
- Runtime-sync command templates and legacy inventory placeholders in relevant
  configuration presets are rejected at their source instead of failing only
  during later composition.

## API and CLI changes

- The ambiguous `POST /api/v1/runtime-config/patch` endpoint is removed.
- New endpoints provide the per-VPS workspace, single preview/apply, and Bulk
  preview/apply contracts. Direct API consumers must update together with this
  release; there is no legacy request-shape fallback.
- `vpsctl config-patch` now performs server preview first and requires the
  reviewed preview hash for confirmed apply.
- ConfigRead job output changes from the former TOML/bootstrap-oriented object
  to `{ type, status, scope, runtime_config }`.
